text_fc9ba5dcd225: Toggle the reference lines with Railway network. Unknown is grey (#4A4A4A), DB InfaGo construction grey-brown (#8b8378) and dashed, outside the DB InfaGo network yellow (#ffff00) and dotted. Personal knowledge and GPS colours appear above it. Reference geometry alone never counts as a trip. The small i below the map opens source and data-version information. Click it again to hide the information.
text_0fb9b3b16771: On Android the rail network is packaged with the app and remains visible without internet. On the web the network file loads on first opening; later offline use requires it to remain in the browser cache. OpenStreetMap background tiles still require internet.
text_0d83493024ae: M1 rail network as a toggleable offline reference layer. Travelled sections remain blue; two passes in each direction turn them green.
text_7a563ef9b8ba: When the last journey was up to 180 days ago, travelled sections stay blue until you have travelled them at least twice in each direction. They then turn green. Older journeys are orange or red as shown in the legend. Each train journey counts at most once per direction for each roughly 100-metre section. Multiple GPS fixes or reloading a journey never increase the count. Only unambiguous matches to the reference network count; gaps and ambiguous matches earn no credit. The calculation uses your own available recordings on the device and server. Without the reference network no green match is possible; known journey dates may still produce orange or red.
